::: {#exm-consistency-birthwt}
#### Consistency of the sample mean for birth weights

The `birthwt` data record the birth weight (grams) of `r nrow(read.csv("data/birthwt.csv"))` babies
from a study at Baystate Medical Center in Springfield, Massachusetts
[@hosmer1989applied]; the data ship with the R package
[`MASS`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=MASS) (`MASS::birthwt`),
and this site has a copy at [`data/birthwt.csv`](data/birthwt.csv).

To see @cor-sample-mean-consistent at work,
treat these babies as a finite population
and let the estimand $\mean$ be their population mean birth weight.
We draw $n$ babies at random with replacement,
so the draws are independent with the population's mean and variance,
and we ask how often the sample mean misses $\mean$
by at least $\varepsilon = 100$ grams.
For each $n$ we repeat the sampling 2000 times
and report the fraction of repeats that miss,
with a 95% confidence interval for that probability
(the Wilson score interval with continuity correction, the default of `prop.test()`),
next to the bound $\varpar / (n \varepsilon^2)$
that @lem-estimation-error-bound gives, capped at 1 because a probability cannot exceed 1,
using $\pMSE{\bar X_n} = \varpar / n$ from [the example on two estimators of a mean](estimation.qmd#exm-mse-sample-mean).

```{r}
#| label: consistency-birthwt-sim
#| code-fold: true
birthwt <- read.csv("data/birthwt.csv")
bwt <- birthwt$bwt

# The population: the 189 observed birth weights.
mu <- mean(bwt)
# Population variance (divisor N, not N - 1), because the draws below
# come from exactly this finite population.
sigma_sq <- mean((bwt - mu)^2)
eps <- 100
n_reps <- 2000
sample_sizes <- c(5, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 320)

set.seed(203)
miss_counts <- vapply(
  sample_sizes,
  function(n) {
    sum(replicate(
      n_reps,
      abs(mean(sample(bwt, n, replace = TRUE)) - mu) >= eps
    ))
  },
  numeric(1)
)

miss_ci <- lapply(miss_counts, prop.test, n = n_reps)

consistency_sim <- data.frame(
  n = sample_sizes,
  miss_prob = miss_counts / n_reps,
  lower = vapply(miss_ci, function(ci) ci$conf.int[1], numeric(1)),
  upper = vapply(miss_ci, function(ci) ci$conf.int[2], numeric(1)),
  bound = pmin(1, sigma_sq / (sample_sizes * eps^2))
)
consistency_sim
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-consistency-birthwt-alt
#| include: false
fig_alt_consistency <- sprintf(
  paste(
    "Line chart with sample size n on a logarithmic horizontal axis",
    "and the probability that the sample mean misses the population mean",
    "by at least 100 grams on the vertical axis.",
    "The simulated probability, with 95%% confidence bands,",
    "falls from %.2f at n = %d to %.3f at n = %d,",
    "and stays below the bound, which also falls toward 0."
  ),
  consistency_sim$miss_prob[1], consistency_sim$n[1],
  consistency_sim$miss_prob[nrow(consistency_sim)],
  consistency_sim$n[nrow(consistency_sim)]
)
```

::: {#fig-consistency-birthwt}

```{r}
#| label: consistency-birthwt-plot
#| fig-alt: !expr fig_alt_consistency
#| code-fold: true
p <- ggplot(consistency_sim, aes(x = n)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = miss_prob, linetype = "simulated")) +
  geom_point(aes(y = miss_prob)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = bound, linetype = "bound")) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = sample_sizes) +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(simulated = "solid", bound = "dashed"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "sample size n",
    y = "probability of a miss"
  )
if (knitr::is_html_output()) plotly::ggplotly(p) else p
```

The chance that the sample mean of $n$ birth weights misses the population mean by 100 g or more,
by simulation (2000 repeats per $n$, with 95% confidence bands) and by the bound from @lem-estimation-error-bound
:::

The simulated probability shrinks toward zero as $n$ grows,
as consistency says it must,
and it lies below the bound at every sample size here,
which is loose for small $n$ but follows the same $1/n$ decay.

:::
